resources.string: HyperOS has settings of its own that stop a closed app from being started. MilO can read only the first of them, and not with certainty. Set each one, then confirm it here.
%1$s is paired, and Android is watching for it.
MilO is exempt from battery optimisation.
\"Pause app activity if unused\" is off for MilO.
MilO measures a trip from GPS positions. Allow precise location.
A trip that starts by itself starts while MilO is closed. Android opens its own location screen for this: choose \"Allow all the time\" there.
The trip notification, and the warning when a trip could not start, need this.
Without it MilO cannot see the truck connect or disconnect.
Location is switched off for the whole phone. No trip can be recorded.
Android may stop MilO to save battery. Allow it to run without battery optimisation.
Recommended. Switch off \"Pause app activity if unused\" for MilO, or Android stops it after months without being opened.
Battery Saver is on. It limits location and background work, so a trip can be missed or cut short.
MilO cannot read this setting. On MilO\'s app page, set Battery saver to \"No restrictions\", then confirm it here.

Recommended. MilO cannot read these. Under \"Other permissions\", switch on \"Show on Lock screen\", the permission to start or open windows in the background, and \"Permanent notification\". Then confirm it here.
MilO cannot read this. Open the recent apps, press and hold MilO\'s card and tap the padlock, so the cleaners leave MilO alone. Then confirm it here.
Allow precise location first, in the row above.
Battery use for MilO is set to Restricted, which blocks trip recording. Change it to Unrestricted on MilO\'s app page.
Android reports that MilO is restricted in the background, which blocks trip recording. On MilO\'s app page, open Battery saver and choose \"No restrictions\".
No truck is paired. Pick it from the phone\'s Bluetooth devices.
%1$s was paired, but Android no longer watches for it. Pair it again.
%1$s is stored as the truck, but this phone cannot watch for a device in the background. Only the Bluetooth signal itself can start a trip.
MilO could not check the pairing. The Log screen says why.
Looks on. MilO reads this through an unofficial check, so it is not a certainty.
Looks off. While it is off, HyperOS does not let the truck wake MilO. Find MilO in the list and switch it on.
MilO could not read this setting. Find MilO in the list and switch it on, then confirm it here.
You confirmed this on %1$s. MilO cannot check it.
MilO watches for one Bluetooth device: the truck. Pick it from the devices this phone is paired with. Android then asks you to allow it.
Until one is, no trip starts by itself.
Paired, and Android is watching for it. A trip starts by itself when it connects.
Paired before, but Android no longer watches for it. Pair it again from the list below.
Stored as the truck, but this phone cannot watch for a device in the background. Only the Bluetooth signal itself can start a trip.
MilO could not check whether Android is watching for it. The Log screen says why.
Waiting for Android. If its dialog is open, choose Allow.
Android\'s dialog was closed without allowing. Nothing was changed. Pick the truck again to retry.
What went wrong: %1$s. Nothing was changed. Check that the truck is paired with this phone in the Bluetooth settings and that Bluetooth and Location are on, then pick it again.
Before you can pick the truck
MilO is not allowed to use Nearby devices. It needs that to list the phone\'s Bluetooth devices and to see the truck connect.
Bluetooth is switched off. Switch it on to see the paired devices.
Location is switched off. Android needs it on to pair the truck with MilO.
No device is paired with this phone. Pair the truck in the phone\'s Bluetooth settings first, then come back.
Picking another device replaces the current truck.
